title: Specialty coffee was renting its audience on Blinkit — a QR in every box turned trial buyers into ₹1,399/month subscribers
content: A Bengaluru specialty-coffee brand (single-origin South Indian beans, ₹549 per 250g) was doing 62% of its ₹38L monthly revenue on Blinkit and Zepto across Bengaluru, Mumbai and Pune. Discovery was strong but the buyers were invisible: no email, no phone, only ~9% reordered next month, and platform commission plus ad fees ate 31% of MRP. The founder wanted to scale quick-commerce spend; the real problem was that none of it built an asset. Three moves: every order shipped a QR insert giving 20% off the first direct subscription plus a free ceramic dripper on the website; a WhatsApp replenishment flow nudged at day 22, when a 250g bag runs out for a daily drinker; and ₹1.8L/month of Meta retargeting was aimed only at the pin codes where quick-commerce orders spiked. Over five months ~13% of quick-commerce buyers scanned the QR and 41% of scanners subscribed at ₹1,399/month (two bags), adding ~2,150 subscribers. Direct revenue went from 12% to 29% of total, blended CAC fell from ₹690 to ₹430, and 6-month subscriber retention hit 68%.
lesson: Quick-commerce is paid discovery, not a customer base — Blinkit and Zepto own the buyer, you just rent the shelf. Put a concrete reason-to-leave-the-platform (a real discount plus a one-time gift) in every physical box, then own the predictable replenishment moment on WhatsApp. The box is your cheapest acquisition channel and the run-out date is your conversion trigger.
